name: NORTH KOREA

flag.title: Flag of N. Korea
flag.note: Red star on white disc, broad red band

lead: North Korea is the northern half of a peninsula between China and Japan. It is one of the most secretive countries on Earth. The Kim family has ruled it since 1948.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: About 80% of North Korea is mountains. The Nangnim and Hamgyong ranges run down it like a spine.
Mount Paektu, on the Chinese border, is a sacred, sleeping volcano with a crater lake called Heaven Lake. The lake is 384 m deep.
animals: The Asiatic black bear lives in the cold northern forests. A white crescent on its chest earns it the name moon bear.
The Korean water deer lives in river marshes. Unlike most deer, males have no antlers. Instead they grow long curved fangs below the lip.
culture: Every year the Mass Games fill the world's biggest stadium, in the capital Pyongyang. Over 100,000 dancers and gymnasts move in perfect unison.
Schoolchildren spend hundreds of hours studying the ruling Kim family. Citizens once had to pick a hairstyle from just 28 government-approved cuts.
history: Korea was one kingdom for over a thousand years. Japan took control in 1910. After 1945, the Soviet Union (a giant state led by Russia) backed the North. The United States backed the South.
The Korean War (1950–53) ended in a ceasefire (a stop to the fighting), not a peace treaty. So the two Koreas are technically still at war. Kim Jong Un has led since 2011.
wows: North Korea dropped its own Juche calendar for the world's usual one in 2024.
Pyongyang's 105-storey Ryugyong Hotel has stood since 1987 but never opened.
Mount Paektu's AD 946 eruption, one of history's biggest, sent ash to Japan.
North Korea moved its clocks 30 minutes in 2015 for independence, then back in 2018 for peace.
At the Mass Games, 30,000 schoolchildren flip cards to make the world's biggest living picture.
North Korea has its own internet, Kwangmyong, completely separate from the world's web.
The DMZ, the strip between the two Koreas, is undisturbed after 70+ years and now a wildlife sanctuary.

myths.myth: North and South Korea speak different languages
myths.fact: Both speak Korean. Only some words and accents differ, like British and American English.

myths.myth: Bears sleep so deeply in winter that nothing wakes them
myths.fact: Bears sleep lightly and wake easily. Mother bears even give birth during their winter sleep.
